question: Which fact is correct about the rotational speed of the Earth?
options: Remains the same at all places
Maximum at the equator and minimum at the poles
Maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator
Only in the oceans is it higher
solution: The Earth's rotation speed varies with latitude. It occurs fastest at the equator because there the Earth has to travel the greatest distance. As we move towards the poles, this speed decreases.

question: What is the condition in the Northern Hemisphere during the 'Summer Solstice'?
options: 6 months of night begins at the North Pole
The longest day occurs on December 22.
The longest day is on June 21
solution: On the summer solstice (June 21), the Sun is perpendicular to the Tropic of Cancer. In contrast, on the winter solstice (December 22) the Sun shines directly on the Tropic of Capricorn.

question: What is the real astronomical meaning of 'Blue Moon'?
options: The occurrence of two full moons in the same calendar month
When the Moon is eclipsed it is called Red Moon.
The first full moon of the year
When the Moon looks blue due to dust
solution: Blue Moon is a rare phenomenon that occurs approximately once every 2-3 years. There is also an idiom 'Once in a blue moon', which means a very rare event.

question: Which statement is correct about the 'Great Circle'?
options: It divides the Earth into two equal hemispheres
It divides the Earth into only four parts
solution: The equator (0° latitude) is the largest latitude circle. Aircraft and ships often use the 'Great Circle Route' to save fuel and time as it is the shortest distance between two points.

question: Between which lines is the 'Temperate Zone' located?
options: Between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle (in the north)
Between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer, this is the tropical (Torrid) region.
This is the frigid region between the Arctic Circle and the poles.
solution: There are four distinct seasons in the temperate zone. The climate here is considered most suitable for human habitation.

question: When does 'Supermoon' occur?
options: When there are two full moons in a month it is called 'Blue Moon'.
When the Moon hides behind the Sun, it is the state of eclipse.
When the Moon is closest to the Earth in its orbit (Perigee) at the time of full moon, in this situation the Moon appears 14% larger and 30% brighter than normal.
solution: The term supermoon is used for 'Perigee-Syzygy'. This occurs astronomically when the Moon is at its minimum distance from the Earth.

question: Why are latitude lines called 'parallels'?
options: Because they have the same length
Because they are parallel to the sun's rays
Because they are equivalent to longitudes
Because they never intersect each other
solution: Latitude lines are perfect circles (except at the poles). The circumference of the circles becomes smaller as we move towards the poles but the distance of 111 km between them remains constant.

question: Which eclipse is likely to occur at the time of 'Conjunction Syzygy'?
solution: The conjunction occurs on the day of Amavasya (New Moon). However, not every Amavasya sees an eclipse because the Moon's orbit is inclined by 5° to the Earth's orbit.

question: Which statement is incorrect regarding the 'Great Circle'?
options: This is the shortest route for airplane flights
It divides the Earth into two equal hemispheres
All longitudes (along with opposite longitudes) form the Great Circle
solution: The great circle is the largest possible circle that can be drawn on the Earth's surface. The equator is the most prominent example of this.

question: By what other names are longitudes known?
solution: Lines of longitude are semicircular lines drawn from pole to pole. Two opposite longitudes (such as 0° and 180°) together form a great circle.

question: Why is 'Gulf of Kutch' important for Tidal Energy in India?
options: Tidal range is maximum here. Due to the narrow shape of the bay, the tidal water rises very high, which is suitable for generating electricity.
The water is very cold here
solution: The coast of Gujarat receives the highest tidal waves in India due to its topography. Gulf of Khambhat and Gulf of Kutch are its main centres.

question: In case of Lunar Eclipse, which body is in the middle?
solution: Lunar eclipse occurs only on the day of full moon. This is also called the state of 'Viyuti' (Opposition).

question: What happens if you cross the International Date Line (IDL) westward (e.g. US to Australia)?
options: You lose a day (Lose a day / Date is added by 1)
solution: Westbound: The date is shifted by +1 day (e.g. Monday directly to Tuesday). This is called 'losing a day' because you 'gave up' those 24 hours of travel.

question: What is approximately the difference between the Earth's Equatorial Radii and Polar Radii?
solution: Earth's equatorial radius (6378 km) is larger than its polar radius (6357 km). For this reason the equatorial circumference is also greater than the polar circumference. This is all due to the Earth's bulge at the equator.

question: What is the time difference between 'High Tide' and 'Low Tide'?
solution: The timing of tides changes every day because the Moon is also revolving around the Earth. That is why tomorrow's tide will be late by about 50 minutes compared to today's.

question: When do 'Spring Tides' come?
options: When the Sun, Moon and Earth are in a straight line (Syzygy)
Despite the name, these tides occur every new and full moon throughout the year.
When the Earth is farthest from the Sun
When the Moon and the Sun are at right angles to each other (Quadrature)
solution: The name of spring tides comes from 'Spring' (to jump). At this time, high tides are very high and low tides are very low, that is, the tidal range is maximum.

question: Where does 'Longitude' measure the angular distance of a place?
options: Latitude is measured from the Equator.
solution: Lines of longitude are narrower at the poles and wider at the equator. These are used to determine time and know the exact position.

question: Which country has the most time zones in the world?
solution: Russia is the largest country in the world, but the islands of France are spread across different longitudes around the world, so it has more time zones.

question: What does 'Perigee' mean in the context of the Moon?
options: When the Moon is closest to the Earth
When the Moon is farthest from the Earth, this position is called 'Apogee'.
When an eclipse occurs on the Moon, it is called a lunar eclipse.
When the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, it can be called the position or conjunction of a solar eclipse (Syzygy).
solution: At the time of perigee, the Moon's tidal force is greater, causing high tides in the ocean. In contrast, the height of the tide is less at the time of apogee.

question: What is the science of measuring and understanding the exact geometric shape of the Earth, its orientation in space and gravitational field called?
solution: Earth is studied at different levels. While geography looks at general features, geodesy uses advanced techniques to understand the actual physical and mathematical shape of the Earth. It is essential for navigation and satellite data.

question: The whole world is divided into how many time zones?
solution: Each time zone is typically 15° longitude wide. However, some large countries have more than one time zone.

question: What is the main reason for tides in the sea?
options: Gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun
solution: Tides are the regular rise and fall of water levels. Although the Sun is much larger than the Moon, the Moon is more effective in causing tides because it is much closer to the Earth.

question: What is the 'Polar Circumference' of the Earth?
solution: Due to the geoid shape of the Earth, the circle around the equator is about 68 km larger than the circle through the poles.

question: When does the state of 'Equinox' occur in a year?
solution: March 21 is called 'Vernal Equinox' and September 23 is called 'Autumnal Equinox'. At this time none of the Earth's poles is inclined towards the Sun.

question: What does 'Semi-Diurnal Tides' mean?
options: There are two high tides and two low tides during the day, each cycle lasting approximately 12 hours and 26 minutes. It is common in most parts of the world.
Tides occur only once a month
Tide coming only once a day
solution: The time interval between two consecutive high tides is 12 hours 25 minutes. This is due to the combined effect of the Earth's rotation and the Moon's revolution.

question: On which date does 'Autumnal Equinox' occur?
solution: At the time of Equinox, day and night are exactly equal. This is the situation twice a year when the inclination of the Sun is zero.

question: What is the reason for the phenomenon of 'Red Moon' (Blood Moon)?
options: Direct fall of the sun's rays
solution: When the Earth blocks sunlight, the red light filtered through the atmosphere gives the Moon a coppery red color. This is called 'blood moon'.

question: What is the position of 'Sizigi' called in which the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon?
solution: During opposition the Moon receives complete sunlight from the Earth (full moon). If they are in a perfect line, the Earth's shadow covers the Moon.

question: What is true about longitude 180° East and 180° West?
options: These meet at the Tropic of Cancer
These are parallel to the equator
These two are the same line
solution: 180° longitude was chosen as the International Date Line because it passes through the mostly uninhabited Pacific Ocean.

question: In which direction does the Earth rotate on its axis?
solution: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in 23 hours 56 minutes and 4 seconds. This is called rotation. Due to this rotation, the phenomena of day and night occur on Earth.

question: What is the main reason for day and night on Earth?
options: Rotation of the Earth on its axis
Revolution of the Earth around the Sun
solution: Rotation is the process by which the Earth rotates once in 24 hours. Revolution is a journey of 365 days around the Sun. These two should not be confused. Rotation = day/night, revolution = year/season.

question: In terms of time calculation, 15° longitude is equal to how much time?
solution: Time Calculation: 360° = 24 hours, 15° = 1 hour, 1° = 4 minutes. If you move towards East, time increases, and if you move towards West, time decreases.

question: Which statement is true about latitude lines?
options: These are imaginary horizontal lines running from east to west.
These are lines running from north to south.
The distance between latitudes decreases as we go towards the poles.
solution: Latitude lines are imaginary lines. The distance between two latitudes is 1° = 111 km. These lines become shorter towards the poles but the distance between them remains constant.

question: Why is the actual shape of the Earth 'Geoid' or 'Oblate Spheroid'?
options: Centrifugal force generated due to the rotation of the Earth
Causes of the Moon's Tidal Force
Causes of the Sun's Gravitational Pull
solution: The Earth is not completely round. The centrifugal force generated due to rotation on its axis pushes it slightly outwards at the Equator and it becomes flat at the poles. This specific shape is called a 'geoid'.

question: In which heat zone of the Earth do the sun's rays always fall obliquely?
options: Frigid Zone: Here the rays are so oblique that very little heat reaches them.
solution: The temperate zone is located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle (north) and between the Tropic of Capricorn and the Antarctic Circle (south).

question: 'Prime Meridian' (0°) passes through which European country?
solution: Greenwich was accepted as the prime meridian at a conference held in Washington DC in 1884.

question: When does the situation of 'Neap Tides' occur?
options: When the Sun and the Moon are at right angles with respect to the Earth
When only the force of the Sun acts
When the Moon is closest to the Earth
solution: During neap tide the height of the tide is lower than normal because the Sun and Moon partially balance each other's pull.

question: Which fact is wrong regarding 'Equator'?
options: It is also called the 'Great Circle'
This is the smallest latitude circle.
It divides the Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres
Here the length of day and night is almost equal
solution: The Equator (0°) is the most important latitude of the Earth. It is also called 'equator line'. As we move away from the equator, the size of the latitude circles becomes smaller.

question: Which part of the shadow is 'Umbra'?
options: The part where only red light is visible
solution: A total solar eclipse can be seen only in those areas where the Moon's 'umbra' touches the Earth's surface.

question: When does 'Annular Solar Eclipse' occur?
options: When the Moon is very close, a 'Total Solar Eclipse' occurs.
When the Earth is very close to the Sun
When the Sun turns blue the color of the Sun does not change, only the visibility changes.
When the Moon is away from the Earth (Apogee) and cannot completely cover the Sun, at this time the Sun looks like a 'Ring of Fire'.
solution: In an annular eclipse the angular diameter of the Moon is smaller than that of the Sun, so the edge of the Sun appears as a bright ring.

question: What is the effect of the direction of Earth's rotation being 'west to east'?
options: The length of day and night is always equal
The Earth's shape has become perfectly round
The Sun, Moon and stars appear to rise in the east
solution: If the Earth rotated from east to west, our entire time cycle and sense of direction would change. When seen from space, the Earth appears to rotate 'anti-clockwise'.

question: What is the total number of latitudes and what is the total number of latitude circles?
solution: 0° (Equator) + 90 North Latitude + 90 South Latitude = 181. Since the North Pole and South Pole are only points, they are not considered circles, hence the number of circles is 181 – 2 = 179.

question: What is the 'Polar Radius' of the Earth?
solution: Radius is the distance from the center to the surface. Due to Earth's rotation the poles have moved slightly closer to the center, so the polar radius is smaller.

question: The state of 'Sizigi' that occurs during a solar eclipse?
solution: Conjunction always occurs on the day of Amavasya (New Moon), which is a necessary condition of solar eclipse.

question: How is the position of 'Quadrature' related to tides?
options: At this time the sea dries up
solution: On the Saptami/Ashtami of Shukla Paksha and Krishna Paksha of the Moon, a situation of 'Quadrature' is formed, due to which the lowest height tides occur in the sea.

question: Which statement is correct with reference to the situation in India?
solution: The Earth is divided by the Equator into North/South and the Prime Meridian into East/West. The latitudinal position of India is north and the longitudinal position is east, hence it is in the north-eastern hemisphere.

question: What is 'Tidal Range'?
options: The time interval of arrival of tides is called the tidal cycle.
Water level difference between high tide and low tide
The total depth of the sea is called bathymetry.
solution: The tidal range depends on coastal shapes. The 'Gulf of Kutch' in Gujarat in India has the maximum potential for tidal energy because the structure there increases the height of the tide.

question: What is the situation in the Southern Hemisphere at the time of 'Makar Sankranti'?
options: It is winter in the Northern Hemisphere
The shortest night occurs on 22 December
The longest day is on December 22. On this day the Sun shines directly on the Tropic of Capricorn, causing summer in the Southern Hemisphere.
solution: The winter solstice (in the context of the Northern Hemisphere) occurs on December 22. At this time there is 'Midnight Sun' situation in Antarctica.

question: What is the average period of the 'Tidal Cycle'?
solution: The additional delay of 52 minutes occurs because the Moon moves further in its orbit as the Earth rotates, and the Earth has to rotate another 52 minutes to bring that point back in front of the Moon.

question: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Geoid'?
solution: Earth is also called 'Oblate Spheroid'. Geoid refers to the irregular shape it would take if the ocean floor were spread out over the entire Earth.

question: If it is 12 noon at Greenwich (0°), what will be the time at 30° East longitude?
solution: Formula to find time: Longitude difference * 4 minutes. Direction East (+) and West (-). This question is often asked in competitive examinations.

question: What are 'Umbra' and 'Penumbra'?
options: Parts of the shadow formed during an eclipse
solution: During a solar eclipse, people who are in the 'Umbra' region see a total solar eclipse. Those in the 'penumbra' region see a partial solar eclipse.

question: How will the eclipse appear to a person standing in the 'penumbra' area?
options: He will see only red light
solution: Penumbra is the area where the light source is only partially blocked. Most eclipses are only partially visible.

question: What is the difference between 'Flood Tide' and 'Ebb Tide'?
options: Ebb tide occurs only in tsunami
Tide is rising water, ebb is falling water
Both are names of the same process
Tides come only in the rainy season
solution: When the water level rises and comes towards the shore, it is called 'Flood Tide'. When water falls and moves away from the shore, it is called 'Ebb Tide'.

question: How does it change as we move from 32 km) towards the poles?
options: It continuously decreases and becomes 0 at the poles
solution: This is why longitudes are more effectively used to measure 'time' and 'angle' rather than measuring 'distance'.

question: What do 'isochrones' represent?
options: Places with equal temperature are called 'isotherms'.
Lines connecting places with equal travel time from a common center
Places with uniform rainfall are called 'isohyets'.
solution: Isochrons are used in transportation planning to determine how long it takes to reach different areas from a center.

question: What effect does the position of the Moon's 'apogee' have on tides?
options: The height of the tide decreases
The height of the tide increases
solution: When the Moon is apogee (farthest), its 'tidal raising force' is weak.

question: What is the meaning of 'Meridian'?
solution: AM (Ante Meridiem) = Before Noon, PM (Post Meridiem) = After Noon. All these words are inspired by 'Meridian' (longitude).

question: Why is the International Date Line (IDL) zig-zag?
options: Due to the depth of the sea
So that puts some island groups and countries in the same time zone and date
solution: The date line is bent near the Bering Strait, Fiji, Tonga and other islands. It is made on the basis of 180° longitude.

question: 'Perihelion' is the situation when the Earth is closest to the Sun. On what date does it happen?
solution: Perihelion and aphelion are caused by the elliptical orbit of the Earth. The distance at perihelion is 147 million km and at aphelion it is 152 million km.

question: What is the Earth's rotation period of 23 hours 56 minutes and 4 seconds called?
solution: The Earth has to rotate a little more (4 minutes) to return to the same position relative to the Sun, so our normal solar day is 24 hours.

question: What is the position of the Moon during a Solar Eclipse?
solution: Solar eclipse always occurs on Amavasya (New Moon). It can be of three types: partial, annular and complete.

question: What is the position of the Sun in the 'Temperate Zone'?
options: The sun does not shine here for 6 months.
Here the sun always rises in the west.
The sun shines overhead twice a year
solution: People living in temperate zone can never see their shadow exactly below their feet (Zero Shadow), because the Sun is always tilted towards south or north.

question: What is the Equatorial Circumference of the Earth?
solution: The circumference of the Earth was first measured by Eratosthenes. The equatorial circumference is approximately 68 km greater than the polar circumference.

question: What would happen if a person crossed the International Date Line eastward (east to west, such as Japan to America)?
options: There is no change in time
He gains a day (Gains a day / Date is subtracted by 1)
There is a difference of only 4 minutes
solution: Crossing the IDL depends on the direction of travel. Eastbound (Japan to USA) = Gain a day (date decreases by one). Westbound (USA to Japan) = Lose a day (date increases by one).

question: Solar eclipse can occur only on which day?
solution: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth. For this the condition of 'Syzygy' and 'Conjunction' is necessary.

question: Why is the Equator considered the 'Great Circle'?
options: Because it has the shortest length
Because the Prime Meridian passes through here
Because it passes through the center of the Earth and divides it into two equal parts
solution: There can be an infinite number of great circles on any sphere, but across latitudes the only great circle is the equator. Two opposite lines of longitude together form a great circle.

question: On which date 'Aphelion' occurs, when the Earth is at its maximum distance from the Sun?
solution: Interestingly, it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere on July 4, when the Earth is farthest from the Sun. This proves that heat does not come from distance, but from axial tilt.

question: Which African countries does the Prime Meridian pass through? (Trick to remember: BSF Game in TOGO)
solution: The Prime Meridian passes through Europe and the continent of Africa. It is also called 'International Meridian'. 'BSF GAME in TOGO' is a great trick to remember this.
